# Bridgeland Builders

> Bridgeland Builders is a Winnipeg renovation contractor for kitchens, bathrooms, basements, whole-home renovations, home additions and commercial fit-ups in Winnipeg and nearby communities. Phone: 431-866-5644. Bridgeland Builders serves Winnipeg and nearby communities within about an hour of the city, including Headingley, East St. Paul, West St. Paul, Oak Bluff, Selkirk and Steinbach.

Renovation and construction contractor based in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada. Not affiliated with Bridgeland, Texas or the Bridgeland neighbourhood of Calgary.

Bridgeland Builders is a service-area renovation and construction contractor based in Winnipeg, Manitoba,
with over 60 years of combined experience and more than 100 completed projects. Quotes are free and
written, every project starts with a free on-site visit, and permits and inspections are coordinated
with the City of Winnipeg or the local municipality when a project requires them.

## Services
- [Basement renovations](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/basement-renovations): Basement development and renovations in Winnipeg: moisture checked first, walls insulated for winter, permits coordinated. Free on-site visit and quote.
- [Basement suites](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/basement-suites): Basement suite renovations in Winnipeg: zoning and permits confirmed first, then entrance, egress, kitchen, bath and separation. Free on-site visit.
- [Bathroom renovations](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/bathroom-renovations): Bathroom renovations in Winnipeg with proper waterproofing under the tile. Most take 2–3 weeks. Start with a free on-site visit and a written quote.
- [Home additions](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/home-additions): Home additions in Winnipeg that match the existing house, with permits, foundation, structure and finishes coordinated. Free on-site visit and quote.
- [Kitchen renovations](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/kitchen-renovations): Kitchen renovations in Winnipeg: layout, cabinets, countertops and lighting, most done in 4–6 weeks. Start with a free on-site visit and written quote.
- [Whole home renovations](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/whole-home-renovations): Whole home renovations in Winnipeg under one plan and one written scope: layout, kitchen, baths, flooring and paint. Most take 8–16 weeks. Free visit.
- [Commercial renovations](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/commercial-renovations): Commercial renovations in Winnipeg for offices, stores, restaurants, hotels and clinics, with a free site visit, written quote and after-hours scheduling.
- [Office renovations](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/office-renovations): Office renovations and fit-ups in Winnipeg, planned around your lease dates and team. Free site visit, written quote, after-hours work, weekly updates.
- [Retail renovations](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/retail-renovations): Retail store renovations and fit-outs in Winnipeg: layouts, storefronts, fitting rooms and finishes, built to your opening date with after-hours work.
- [Restaurants & hospitality](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/restaurant-renovations): Restaurant, café, bar and hotel renovations in Winnipeg, scheduled around service hours and planned for health review. Free site visit and written quote.
- [Medical & dental offices](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/medical-dental-office-renovations): Dental and medical office renovations in Winnipeg: operatories, exam rooms and reception, phased around patient hours. Free site visit and written quote.
- [General contracting](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/general-contracting): General contractor in Winnipeg for home and commercial renovations: trades, schedule, permits and inspections, built to your drawings. Free site visit.
- [Windows and doors installation](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/windows-and-doors): Window and door installation in Winnipeg: same-size replacements, new openings with permits, and clean trim. Free on-site visit and written quote.
- [Exterior painting](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/exterior-painting): Exterior painting in Winnipeg for homes and commercial buildings: careful prep, repairs and weather-planned coats. Free on-site visit and written quote.
- [Masonry & stucco](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/masonry-stucco): Masonry and stucco repair in Winnipeg: cracked stucco, repointing, brick and stone repairs and new finishes. Free on-site visit and written quote.
- [Flooring](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/flooring): Flooring installation in Winnipeg for homes, basements and commercial spaces: removal, subfloor prep and clean trim. Free on-site visit and written quote.
- [Demolition](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/demolition): Interior demolition in Winnipeg: kitchen, bathroom, basement and commercial strip-outs with dust control and haul-away. Free on-site visit and quote.

- [How Much Does a Home Renovation Cost in Canada?](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/home-renovation-cost-canada): Why there’s no reliable national average for what a renovation costs, what Statistics Canada’s construction price data does show, why per-square-foot figures mislead, and how to get a real number for your project.

- [Basement Flooding in Winnipeg: Backwater Valves, Sump Pits and Permits](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/basement-flood-protection-winnipeg): Sewer backup, groundwater and surface water reach a basement in different ways. Here’s how Winnipeg homes are protected, and what to sort out before you finish one.
- [Clay Soil and Basement Cracks in Winnipeg: What’s Normal](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/clay-soil-basement-cracks-winnipeg): Winnipeg’s clay swells and shrinks with moisture, and basements show it. How to read the cracks, when an engineer should look, and how to build finishes that allow for movement.
- [Clinic Renovation Permits in Winnipeg: What to Plan For](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/clinic-renovation-permits-winnipeg): What a medical, dental or physiotherapy clinic renovation in Winnipeg needs before work starts and before patients come back.
- [How Much Should an Ensuite Renovation Cost in Winnipeg?](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/ensuite-renovation-winnipeg): An ensuite costs what its decisions cost: whether the toilet and shower stay where they are, how big the shower is, how much tile goes on the walls and whether the room grows into a closet. Here is how to think those choices through before you ask for a price.
- [When to Paint Your House Exterior in Winnipeg](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/exterior-painting-winnipeg-when-to-paint): Winnipeg's painting season is short, and the weather decides more than the calendar does. Here is how to time an exterior paint job, prepare the surfaces properly and avoid the mistakes that make paint fail early.
- [Home Addition Zoning in Winnipeg: Permits and Variances](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/home-additions-and-zoning-winnipeg): Before an addition is designed, it has to fit two sets of rules: zoning, which decides where and how big you can build, and the building code, which decides how it is built. Here is how both work in Winnipeg, and what changed in 2025.
- [Home Renovation Financing in Canada: Your Options](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/home-renovation-financing-canada): A plain-language comparison of the main ways Canadians finance a renovation, what each one means for risk and flexibility, and which federal programs have closed.
- [Home Renovation Planning in Canada: Guide and Checklist](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/home-renovation-planning-guide-canada): A step-by-step plan for Canadian homeowners: set goals and a budget, understand permits and codes, build a realistic timeline, and run the safety checks that belong before demolition.
- [How to Check a Contractor's WCB Clearance in Manitoba](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/how-to-check-a-contractors-wcb-clearance-manitoba): A WCB clearance letter takes a few minutes to get and tells you whether a contractor is in good standing with the Workers Compensation Board of Manitoba. Here's how to request one.
- [Insulation Rebates in Manitoba: How to Use Them During a Renovation](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/insulation-rebates-during-a-renovation-manitoba): Planning to finish a basement, open up walls or re-side the house? Efficiency Manitoba's Home Insulation Rebate can help with the insulation, but only if the paperwork happens before the demolition does.
- [Home Renovation Grants and Tax Credits in Manitoba](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/manitoba-renovation-tax-credits-rebates): A status check of the renovation tax credits, rebates and loans Manitoba homeowners can still use, the programs that have closed, and the steps that keep a claim valid.
- [Office Fit-Up in Winnipeg: Planning Around Your Lease](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/office-fit-up-lease-planning-winnipeg): How to line up an office fit-up with your lease dates in Winnipeg: what to settle with the landlord, which City approvals apply, and when your team can actually move in.
- [Planning a Winter Basement Development in Winnipeg](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/planning-a-winter-basement-development-winnipeg): Winter suits basement work in Winnipeg: the job is indoors and permit applications avoid the construction-season rush. Here’s how to plan it, month by month.
- [Radon Testing Before Finishing a Basement in Manitoba](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/radon-testing-before-finishing-a-basement): About 19% of Manitobans live in homes above Health Canada’s radon guideline. How to test before you finish a basement, and what to do with the result.
- [Heritage District Renovations: Updating a Character Home in Winnipeg](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/renovating-a-character-home-in-winnipeg): Most older Winnipeg houses are renovated with ordinary permits. A smaller group, on the City's List of Historical Resources or inside a heritage conservation district, needs a heritage permit too. Here is how to tell which applies to your home and how to plan around it.
- [Restaurant Renovation Permits in Winnipeg: What You Need](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/restaurant-renovation-permits-winnipeg): The City, health and liquor approvals a restaurant, café or bar renovation in Winnipeg usually needs, and the order to tackle them in.
- [Secondary Suite Rules in Winnipeg: What the City Requires](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/secondary-suite-rules-winnipeg): Permits, size limits, separation and the 2025 zoning changes for basement and garden suites in Winnipeg, plus the federal programs that do and don’t exist.
- [Spring Flood Prep for Winnipeg Basements: A Homeowner Checklist](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/spring-flood-prep-winnipeg-basements): Snow clearing, sump tests, backwater valves and what to lift off the floor before the spring melt, using City of Winnipeg and Province of Manitoba guidance.
- [What Does a General Contractor Do?](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/what-does-a-general-contractor-do): A plain-language guide for homeowners and business owners: what a general contractor is responsible for, how general contractors price work, and when hiring one makes sense.
- [Window and Door Replacement in Winnipeg: Permits, Glass and Rebates](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/window-and-door-replacement-winnipeg): Replacing windows and doors is one of the more straightforward upgrades for a Winnipeg home, as long as you know when the City needs a permit, what the labels mean and how the rebate works. Here is the short version, checked against official sources.
- [Renovation Permits in Winnipeg: What Needs One and How to Apply](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/winnipeg-renovation-permits): A project-by-project guide to City of Winnipeg building, development, electrical and plumbing permits for home renovations, checked against the City’s own pages.
- [Winnipeg Renovation Show: Questions to Ask Contractors](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/winnipeg-renovation-show-questions-to-ask): How to use the 2027 Winnipeg Renovation Show to build a contractor shortlist: what to bring, what to ask at each booth, and how to compare the answers once you're home.
- [Commercial Interior Design: Balancing Function and Looks](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/how-to-balance-functionality-and-aesthetics-in-a-commercial-space): A practical order of decisions for a commercial interior that works for staff and customers and still looks like your brand, with what to settle early and what can wait.
- [Full vs Partial Renovation: How to Choose for Your Winnipeg Home](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/how-to-choose-between-a-full-renovation-and-partial-upgrades): A full renovation fixes everything at once; partial upgrades spread the work and the cost over time. The right choice depends on the condition of your house, your plans and how much disruption you can live with. Here is a practical way to decide.
- [Commercial Renovation ROI: Which Upgrades Pay Back?](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/understanding-roi-which-commercial-renovations-bring-the-most-value): A plain-language way to judge whether a commercial renovation will pay for itself, which kinds of upgrades tend to earn their cost back, and what quietly eats into the return.

- [How to Choose a Renovation Contractor in Winnipeg](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/how-to-choose-the-right-contractor-for-your-renovation-project): A practical Winnipeg checklist for comparing renovation contractors: what to verify, where to verify it, and what a fair contract and payment schedule look like.

- [Commercial Renovation Planning in Winnipeg: A Business Guide](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/how-to-prepare-your-business-for-a-major-renovation): How to plan a major renovation around a business that needs to keep running: the stages from site visit to occupancy permit, keeping customers informed, and a checklist to start with.
- [Bathroom Renovation Ideas That Add Value in Winnipeg Homes](https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/which-bathroom-remodel-upgrades-offer-the-best-return-on-investment-for-canadian-homeowners): The bathroom upgrades that add value are mostly the ones that keep the room dry, easy to use and easy to clean.
